deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The heading reads roughly 'Bestimmung der Bahn der Vesta aus vier Oertern' (determination of the orbit of Vesta from four places). The page is a numerical test of a set of Vesta elements against the first of four observations. The latest observation is dated February 1809, so the page dates from about 1809. It is unrelated to the elliptic-function work on the neighbouring folios.

(1) TIME REDUCTION (top table). Each row reduces an observed local time to Paris mean time free of light time: t_Paris = t_obs − (light time) − (meridian difference).
- Row 1, 1807 Mar 29: 10h31'16" − 10'26" − 25'51" = 9h54'59". 25'51" is Bremen−Paris (Olbers' observation); 10'26" is the light time.
- Row 2, 1807 Sep 26: 6h53'52" − 23'13" − 27'25" = 6h3'14".
- Row 3, 1808 Jun 22: 13h46'25" − 15'7" − 30'21" = 13h0'57". 30'21" is Göttingen−Paris.
- Row 4, 1809 Feb 16: 7h16'56" − 25'17" − 30'25" = 6h21'18" as written.
The next column converts these to days counted from 1807 Jan 0.0 Paris: 88.413183, 269.252245, 539.542326, 778.264792. The last column gives the observed right ascension and declination, not longitude and latitude:
- α=184°7'38", δ=+11°47'45"
- α=221°15'21", δ=−12°2'59"
- α=353°12'17", δ=−9°12'16"
- α=11°41'10", δ=−0°37'59"

(2) 'ERSTER ORT': SUN FROM SOLAR TABLES.
- Mean longitude: 9s9°42'23.5" (+0.4") + 2s25°45'4.7" + 54'0.3" = 0s6°21'28.9".
- Solar perigee: 9s9°36'17" + 15" = 9s9°36'32".
- Mean anomaly: 0s6°21'29" − 9s9°36'32" = 2s26°44'57" (≈86°44'57").
- Equation of centre: +1°54'37.8", giving 8°16'6.7".
- Small terms from the node (nutation), Moon, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn sum to 54.6". With a further 20.2" (constant or aberration term) the total is 74.8", giving the Sun's longitude 8°17'21.5".
- The integers in columns M, A, B, …, N are table arguments added mod 1000 (e.g. 779+387+4 = 1170 → 170).
- A log radius-vector value 0.9992295 + 921 = 0.9993216 is formed from table corrections.
- Apparent obliquity: ε = 23°27'53.36" − 2.82" + 0.29" = 23°27'50.83".

(3) OBSERVED (α,δ) → ECLIPTIC (λ,β), auxiliary-angle method.
- log tan δ = 9.3198769 and log sin α = 8.8571596 (sin α < 0).
- tan N = tan δ / sin α gives N = 70°59'14.54"; then N + ε = 94°27'5.37".
- tan λ = tan α · cos(N+ε)/cos N, with log tan α = 8.8582873, log cos N = 9.5129898 and log|cos(N+ε)| ≈ 8.8899 (written 8.6899469 in the transcription). This gives log tan λ = 8.2352…, so λ = 179°0'54.35".
- tan β = tan(N+ε) · sin λ: 1.1087421 + 8.2352… gives log tan β = 9.3439913, so β = 12°27'3.30".
- Gauss first wrote 12°26'56.90", struck it and replaced it by 27'3.30".

(4) EPHEMERIS FROM THE ELEMENTS.
- Mean motion n = 978.7216"/day. Check: log n = 2.9906592 = 3.5500066 − (3/2)·0.3728980, with log a = 0.3728980, a ≈ 2.3603.
- Eccentricity angle φ = 5°2'58.1", so e = sin φ ≈ 0.08801 (log e = 8.9445610).
- Mean anomaly: log t = 1.9465170 (t = 88.413183 d), so n·t = 86531.89" = 24°2'11.89".
- Epoch mean anomaly 278°13'41.10" + 24°2'11.89" gives M = 302°15'52.99".
- Kepler's equation E − e sin E = M: e" sin E with log 4.2589861 + 9.9467216 gives −4°27'38.60", so E = 297°48'14.39".
- True anomaly: ½(v−E) = −2°16'49.51" (log sin(φ/2) ≈ 8.6439528 is used), so v = E − 4°33'39.02" = 293°14'35.37".
- Radius vector: log e + log cos E = 8.9445610 + 9.6688036 gives e cos E = 0.04105486. Then log(1 − e cos E) = 9.9817938, and log r = 0.3728980 + 9.9817938 = 0.3546918.
- Argument of latitude: u = v + ω, with ω written as −213°14'50.80" (i.e. ω = 146°45'9.20"). This gives u = 79°59'44.57".
- Node: precession 12.13" (log 9.13725 + 1.94652, i.e. annual precession/365.25 × t) and nutation 17.00" give Ω = 103°12'26.43".
- Inclination: log cos i = 9.9966200 and log sin i = 9.0943971, so i ≈ 7°8'.

(5) HELIOCENTRIC → GEOCENTRIC in an ecliptic frame with x-axis toward the node.
- Planet: log x = log r cos u = 0.3546918 + 9.2398544 = 9.5945462; log y = log r cos i sin u = 0.3513118 + 9.9933457 = 0.3446575; log z = log r sin i sin u = 9.4490889 + 9.9933457 = 9.4424346.
- Sun: longitude minus node = 8°17'21.50" − 103°12'26.43" + 360° = 265°4'55.07". With log R = 9.9997053 this gives log X☉ = 8.9328410 (negative) and log Y☉ = 9.9981034 (negative).
- The sums x + X☉ and y + Y☉ are done with subtraction logarithms: log(1 − 10^(−0.6617052)) = 9.8932518, so log X = 9.4877980; log(1 − 10^(−0.3465541)) = 9.7401716, so log Y = 0.0848291.
- tan(λ−Ω) = Y/X gives λ−Ω = 75°48'24.66", so λ = 179°0'51.09".
- log(ρ cos β) = 0.0848291 − log sin(λ−Ω) (9.9865364) = 0.0982927.
- tan β = z/(ρ cos β), log = 9.3441419, so β = 12°27'18.36".
- Light-time check (my reading of the two small numbers): log ρ ≈ 0.10862 and 0.10862 + 2.6875 gives about 625 s, matching the 10'26" used.

(6) RESIDUALS. Error long. = −3.26" (179°0'51.09" − 179°0'54.35"). Error latit = −15.06" (12°27'3.30" − 12°27'18.36").
errors: Row 4: 7h16'56" − 25'17" − 30'25" = 6h21'14", not 6h21'18". The day fraction 0.264792 corresponds to 6h21'18", which implies a meridian difference of 30'21" (Göttingen−Paris, as in row 3). Either the '25' is a misreading of '21' or it is a slip in writing the meridian correction; the computation downstream is consistent with 30'21".

Sign convention of the residuals is inconsistent. Longitude error −3.26" = computed − observed, but latitude error −15.06" = observed − computed (computed 18.36", observed 3.30"). The convention is not stated, so this may be a slip.
88084.944 − 86531.89 = 1553.054, so the companion number should read 1553.054 (the transcription has 1553.0354). Its purpose is unclear.

Two log radius-vector values appear: 9.9993216 from the table corrections, and 9.9997053, which is actually used in step (5) and agrees with the true Earth–Sun distance of about 0.99934 AU. The relation between them is unclear; not necessarily an error.

Minor last-digit corrections are visible: overwritten log tan λ (8.2352498 vs about 8.2352444 from the stated logs if log|cos(N+ε)| = 8.8899469) and the struck 9.3449275 replaced by 9.3439913. These are routine corrections in the 7-place work.

results.what: Reduction of observation times to Paris mean time, corrected for meridian difference (Bremen 25'51", Göttingen 30'21") and light time, then expressed in days from 1807 Jan 0
Sun's place from solar tables: mean longitude, perigee, equation of centre, planetary perturbations, nutation, obliquity
results.modern_name: solar ephemeris from tables (von Zach/Delambre type)

results.what: Conversion of (α,δ) to (λ,β) via auxiliary angle N: tan N = tan δ/sin α; tan λ = tan α cos(N±ε)/cos N; tan β = tan(N±ε) sin λ

Ephemeris from elliptic elements: n from a via Kepler's third law with Gauss's constant (log k" = 3.5500066), Kepler's equation, true anomaly, radius vector, heliocentric-to-geocentric rectangular coordinates
Use of subtraction logarithms, log(1 − 10^(−d)), to add numbers given by their logs
Comparison of computed and observed geocentric place of Vesta (residuals −3.26" in longitude, −15.06" in latitude) for elements with a ≈ 2.3603, e ≈ 0.0880, i ≈ 7°8', Ω ≈ 103°12', ω ≈ 146°45'

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working sheet from Gauss's well-documented Vesta orbit computations of 1807–1809, published in part in Zach's Monatliche Correspondenz. It reduces observations, computes the Sun's place from tables, converts coordinates, and computes an ephemeris from elements to get residuals. All methods are standard and known to be his, including the Theoria Motus procedures and subtraction logarithms. Its only interest is as a primary source for his numerical practice and the specific elements.

transcription_corrections: Heading: read 'Bestimmung der Bahn der Vesta aus vier Oertern' (fits the content).
'−79 59 44.57' is u = 79°59'44.57" (positive), the argument of latitude.
'179° 0' 54" 430/1125' is the observed longitude 179°0'54.35" (residual −3.26" against 179°0'51.09"); the fraction-like marks are corrections.
Row 4 meridian difference '−30 25' may actually be '−30 21' (the written result 6h21'18" and 0.264792 require 30'21").
The column of numbers after the observation times is days since 1807 Jan 0.0 (Paris), and the last column is right ascension and declination, not ecliptic coordinates.
'☾ [?] 0,1' is a lunar perturbation term of the Sun's longitude; '☊ 17.0' is nutation in longitude.
'0,9992295 … 0.9993216' are log radius-vector values with the characteristic 9 omitted (9.999…).
